tagline: Over Dead Indian Pass the way the Nez Perce slipped through.
intro: Seventeen miles north of Cody, WYO 296 leaves Highway 120 and climbs into the Absaroka Range of the Shoshone National Forest. It crosses Dead Indian Pass, then drops into Sunlight Basin, grizzly country, where a bear is now and then seen near the road in spring. From there it runs on to the Clarks Fork and the Beartooth Highway, 47 miles in all.
In 1877 Chief Joseph led some 700 Nez Perce and 2,000 horses out of Yellowstone and over this ground, with the cavalry waiting on the plains below.

moments.title: Dead Indian Pass
moments.text: Here the Nez Perce milled their horses in a circle, raising dust to look as if they were heading south, then slipped north down a gulch barely two horses wide. The cavalry went south.

moments.title: Sunlight Creek Bridge
moments.text: The highest bridge in Wyoming, built in 1985, carries the road and a walkway on each side across a gorge Sunlight Creek has cut 285 feet deep.

moments.title: Clarks Fork of the Yellowstone
moments.text: The army had ruled out this way down, judging that no trail could lead through. Below the highway bridge, 20.5 miles of the river are now designated Wild.

practical: Unlike the neighboring Beartooth Highway, the Chief Joseph is open in winter.
